main_text.p: refponfumque tuliffet, omnino ita fu-turum: tum Spartam reverfum leges promulgaffe, & non folum iniquum fed etiam nefarium judicaffe, qui legi-bus à Pythio probatis obfequium ab-nueret. Plutarchus verò memorat, quod prætereundum non eft, cum confum-matam jam totam rem Lycurgus ha-beret, effentq; omnia in ufum recepta, ufuque plurium annorum probata, hoc eum velut ftratagema ufurpaffe[?] : vo-caffe nimirum omnes ad concionem, & dixiffe, habere quidem ea, quæ con-ftituta receptaque jam fint, rectè ad in-ferendam alendamque virtutem, & conciliandam civitati profperam for-tunam, fed, quod præcipuum & maxi-mum putaret, id fe non ante editurum quàm Deum confuluiffet: quapropter oportere eos his, quæ conftituta jam effent, fine vitio infiftere, nec mutare aut movere quicquam, quoad ipfe Del-phis domum revertiffet: tum, quod-cunque intellexiffet placere Deo, id fe effe facturum. quam orationem cum collaudaffent omnes, juffiffentque eum Delphos ire, jurejurando ipfum obftrin-xiffe reges primum ac fenatum, deinde & populum univerfum, ad præftanda ea, quæ promitterent,, ac tunc ftatim Delphos profectum, peractis ibi facris ex

page.notes: The mark after "ufurpaffe" and the dash-like mark after "virtutem" are doubtful abbreviation or punctuation signs; they are transcribed as best read. The running head and page number are read from a small scan; "222" is uncertain. Printed "promitterent,," has a doubled comma as printed.
